newsitem.title: PERU: Peru guerrillas still hold up to 300 hostages.
newsitem.headline: Peru guerrillas still hold up to 300 hostages.

text.p: Peruvian guerrillas who stormed the Japanese ambassador's residence were holding between 250 and 300 hostages early Wednesday, said Sally Bowen, the president of Peru's foreign press association who was released from the building.
She said she had seen between 10 and 12 guerrillas inside but believed there were more.
Bowen said the incident began with an explosion then firing from outside into the building. "It was scary, especially during the shooting at the beginning," she said.
She added that the guerrillas who came in forced the hostages to lie face down for 40 minutes. The guerrillas claimed their operation was called "Breaking The Silence."

They demanded that the government release the estimated 400 to 500 Tupac Amaru Revolutionary Movement (MRTA) guerillas in prison, including leader Victor Polai; a review of Peru's judicial system and the beginning of negotiations with the government on Wednesday morning.
Bowen said Japanese Ambassador Morihisa Aoki offered to remain as the only hostage but that offer was rejected by the rebels.
